jurisdiction.venue: U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado

headline: S.E.C. Accuses Eight Rotating Colorado Shell Firms of Printing Fake S.E.C. Certificates in $37.4 Million Crypto Scheme
deck: Regulators allege four consecutive adviser-and-exchange pairings lured 1,500 U.S. investors from WhatsApp stock chats into bogus token platforms, citing real EDGAR filings to project legitimacy.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: SEC civil fraud complaint against eight Colorado entities over alleged $37.4M rotating fake crypto platform ring targeting 1,500+ retail investors.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Printing counterfeit municipal business permits to run a $15,000 pop-up raffle
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Immediate local arrest and state felony forgery counts

sources.title: SEC Charges Eight Entities That Used Fake Crypto Asset Trading Platforms to Steal More Than $37 Million from U.S. Investors (Press Release 2026-115)

interactive_art_spec.caption: The Byron White United States Courthouse in Denver. The S.E.C. filed civil fraud charges in the District of Colorado against eight entities accused of cycling through four bogus crypto trading platforms.
